stories.headline: FrP national conference erupts in racist-remarks scandal as Listhaug battles Støre over party identity
stories.summary: Fremskrittspartiet's annual landsmøte was dominated by a political firestorm: TV2 revealed FrP Storting adviser Hårek Hansen had described Pakistanis as 'minus variants' in a covertly recorded pub conversation. PM Støre demanded Listhaug condemn the remarks as racism; Listhaug initially handled it as an internal personnel matter before eventually, under intense pressure, calling the statements racist on the landsmøte floor. Listhaug was re-elected as FrP leader by acclamation. The broader week also featured Listhaug's landsmøte speech labelling Ap headquarters a 'troll factory,' Støre accusing FrP of borrowing 'far-right American tactics,' and opposition claims that Støre has made lying a 'working method.'

stories.headline: Finance Minister Stoltenberg warns fuel-tax cuts likely illegal under EEA rules as they take effect May 1
stories.summary: A political battle unfolded over Stortinget-mandated cuts to diesel and CO₂ fuel taxes: Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg repeatedly warned the cuts were likely illegal state aid under EEA rules, protested publicly, and refused to give access to his dialogue with the ESA watchdog. The cuts took effect 1 May after Høyre's brief attempt to pause them collapsed; 'Dieselbrølet' industry protesters met Støre and Stoltenberg. Business groups warned of potential repayment liability. FrP claimed credit for the cuts while accusing Stoltenberg of undermining Stortinget's authority.

stories.headline: Støre meets Zelenskyy in Yerevan on the sidelines of European Political Community summit
stories.summary: Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Yerevan, Armenia, where both were attending a European Political Community meeting. Topics included Norway's nearly $1 billion contribution to the PURL program for Ukraine, drone cooperation, and winter gas supplies. Zelenskyy also met the PMs of Finland, the UK, and Czechia.

stories.headline: NBIM annual investment conference in Oslo draws JPMorgan CEO Dimon; Palestinian protesters chain themselves to Norges Bank entrance
stories.summary: The Government Pension Fund Global's annual investment conference in Oslo featured JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon in conversation with NBIM chief Nicolai Tangen, warning about private credit risks, geopolitical fragmentation, and potential bond crises. Citadel's Ken Griffin also spoke, publicly criticizing NYC mayor Mamdani. On the day of the conference, pro-Palestinian activists chained themselves to the entrance of Norges Bank protesting the fund's holdings in Israeli-linked companies.

stories.headline: Norway's first Leopard 2A8 tanks arrive at Rena leir
stories.summary: The first of Norway's 54 Leopard 2A8 NO main battle tanks were delivered and presented at Rena leir in Innlandet. Defence Minister Tore O. Sandvik attended the ceremony; the military described the tank as the world's best and said all 54 would be delivered by 2028 to form the core of Brigade Nord.

stories.headline: Norges Bank interest rate decision: market split 50/50 on May hike amid persistent inflation
stories.summary: Markets and analysts are divided ahead of Norges Bank's scheduled rate announcement, with probability of a May hike at around 50 percent. Sticky domestic inflation in the 3–4 percent range and a wage growth peak have reversed earlier expectations of rate cuts, and forecasters now see the policy rate rising to 4.5 percent by autumn from the current 4 percent.

stories.headline: Equinor advances Bay du Nord offshore Canada with FEED contracts as oil majors eye Canadian acquisitions
stories.summary: Equinor awarded front-end engineering and design (FEED) contracts to BW Offshore and the Subsea Integration Alliance for the $12–14 billion Bay du Nord deepwater project off Newfoundland, targeting a final investment decision in 2027. Concurrently, Reuters reporting cited Equinor—alongside TotalEnergies, BP, and ConocoPhillips—as eyeing acquisition targets in Canada amid post-Middle East-war energy demand.

stories.headline: Norwegian offshore wage talks collapse; state mediator called in to avert output-threatening strike
stories.summary: Wage negotiations between Norwegian oil companies and labour unions broke down Wednesday, triggering a shift to state-led mediation. If the government-appointed mediator fails, workers—including those at Equinor, Aker BP, ConocoPhillips, and Vår Energi—would be eligible to strike, potentially disrupting Norway's roughly 4 million barrels per day of oil equivalent production.

stories.headline: Barth Eide addresses UN Security Council on Gaza and Middle East as Norway chairs AHLC
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide spoke at a UN Security Council ministerial meeting on the Middle East, stating that the Trump peace plan for Gaza is conditioned on Hamas disarmament as a sequential process, and calling on Israel to lift restrictions on aid. Eide chairs the Ad Hoc Liaison Committee, which met in Brussels beforehand with US and EU representatives. Barth Eide also participated in a Nordic-Baltic (NB8) foreign ministers' meeting in Kuressaare, Estonia.

stories.headline: E-tjenesten to recruit new chief; Forsvaret opens process to non-military candidates for first time
stories.summary: Intelligence chief Nils Andreas Stensønes is retiring after six years heading the Norwegian Intelligence Service. For the first time in the service's history, Forsvaret has opened the position to candidates without a military background, stating it seeks the best candidate regardless of background.

stories.headline: Støre gives May Day speech in Sulitjelma mining town, signals openness to new mineral extraction
stories.summary: Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre was the first sitting PM to give a 1 May speech in the historic mining town of Sulitjelma in Nordland. He highlighted the mineral sector as critical for Norwegian security and the green transition, and expressed openness to reopening mining in the area—framing it as aligned with labour movement values.

stories.headline: Norwegian defence corruption risk flagged as military buildup accelerates; three Forsvarsmateriell officials charged
stories.summary: Aftenposten reported that rapidly rising global defence spending—sharpest in Europe—is creating elevated corruption risk, noting that Norwegian economic crime police (Økokrim) recently warned of the trend and three leaders at Forsvarsmateriell were charged with gross breach of trust. Defence Minister Sandvik separately faced Storting scrutiny over multiple scandals including F-16 deliveries to Ukraine, financial irregularities, and a controversial mask purchase.

stories.headline: Norges Bank announces end to new 1000-krone banknote orders and launches central bank certificates
stories.summary: Norges Bank announced it will retain the 1000-krone note as legal tender but banks may no longer order new ones, gradually reducing circulation. Separately, Norges Bank confirmed the launch of central bank certificates as a new liquidity management instrument starting 5 May 2026, following a decision in autumn 2025.

stories.headline: Norwegian Armed Forces expanding conscription intake amid declining recruits' fitness levels
stories.summary: NRK reported that the Norwegian Armed Forces plans to induct 4,600 more soldiers into national service by 2036 in line with the long-term defence plan, but faces a concerning trend of declining physical fitness among draft-age Norwegians. Forsvaret wants more physical testing and activity in schools to address the gap.

stories.headline: Norges Bank raises daily krone purchases to NOK 224 million in May
stories.summary: Norges Bank announced it will increase its daily krone purchases in the foreign exchange market to NOK 224 million in May, up from NOK 174 million in April. The April reduction had followed high oil and gas prices tied to the Middle East war; the increase reflects changed revenue flows.
